questions.q: The aged require specialized care and attention as he grow older.
o: The aged require specialized
as he grow older
questions.s:
When ‘the’ is used before an adjective, the adjective becomes a plural common noun. It will hence take a plural verb. These adjectives are: Rich, poor, needy, aged, blind, dead, meek, wicked, etc. The correct option is (c) "as he grow older."

The correct sentence should be: "The aged require specialized care and attention as they grow older."

One should work hard than others to succeed.

questions.s: When comparing the effort one puts in with others, the comparative form "harder" should be used instead of "hard."

questions.q: One must care as for family members as possible.
questions.s:
(d) Explanation :- Inn dono ke meanings ek hi hai bas structure ka difference hai:-

'One must care for family members as much as possible' = 'One must care as much for family members as possible'

Simile me positive degree ka hi use hota hai isliye much hi sahi hai more and most nhi.

questions.q: The project is so complex as, if not more complex than, we anticipated.
o: if not more complex than
The project is so complex as,
questions.s:
The correct option is (d) "The project is so complex as."

In English, when comparing degrees of complexity, "as...as" is used with positive degree adjectives and "than" with comparative degree adjectives. Therefore, "so complex as" should be replaced with "as complex as"

The corrected sentence should be: "The project is as complex as, if not more complex than, we anticipated."

questions.q: These days, job opportunities are not as better (1)/ as they used to be (2)/ in the early 70's. (3)/ No error (4)
o: These days, job opportunities are not as better
questions.s:
After “as…as”, we use the positive degree of the adjective.
Replace "better” with “good”.

questions.q: (a) Mumbai is /(b) further from /(c) Delhi than /(d) Patna. (e) No error
Manoj is so (credible) that he immediately believed my story.
questions.s: Credulous = an adjective describing a person who easily believes anything.

questions.q: He runs (a) / very fastly (b) / in races. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Fastly' is incorrect; the correct adverb is 'fast.' Answer: (b). 'Fastly' galat hai, sahi adverb hai 'fast.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: (a) Whole the chapter /(b) is full of printing errors which are the outcome /(c) of the proof reader’s carelessness. (d) No error
They prefer living in the countryside than living in the city.
o: than living in the city
questions.s:
The ‘Preferable’ Adjective is used in only a comparative degree. ‘Preferable’ is followed by ‘to’ and not ‘than’ or ‘more’. Prefer’ (verb) is followed by ‘to’ and not ‘than’. Therefore, "than living in the city" should be corrected to "to living in the city."

The corrected sentence would be: "They prefer living in the countryside to living in the city."

questions.q:
Choose the correct form of adjective for the given sentence:
She is very _______; you never know what she is going to do next.
questions.s:
The sentence describes someone whose actions cannot be guessed and who may do anything next. The adjective that expresses this quality is:
unpredictable= not possible to know what she will do next

questions.q:
Choose the correct form of adjective for the given sentence:
Sanjana is determined to get what she wants and in the process she does not mind even if she hurts people. She is______.
questions.s:
The adjective must express the quality shown in the sentence.
Here, Sanjana hurts others without feeling bad just to achieve what she wants.
The adjective that shows cruel / pitiless behaviour is:
Ruthless= without pity; hurting others for one’s own benefit

questions.s:
The correct answer is option a.

The correct sentence would be: “This is the most challenging task I have ever encountered.”

Here we are comparing the task to all other tasks. So, superlative degree should be come in place of challenge.

Hence, “most challenging” is the most appropriate answer.

questions.q: My neighbours were serious injured in the car accident.
questions.s:
Serious” is an adjective, but we should use an adverb before a past participle (injured).
So “seriously injured” is correct.

questions.q:

_______of living life on his own terms, he made few compromises.
questions.s:
Desirous of” is the correct adjective phrase meaning “wanting/keen to do something.”
So the correct sentence is: Desirous of living life on his own terms, he made few compromises.
